headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5. Mandates delivery of unexpended property to minor at age 21 (or 18 for non-donor transfers upon request), to estate upon death, or to conservator if incapacitated.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6. Imposes fiduciary duty to act in minor's interest without conflicts, applying Missouri prudent investor act (sections 469.900 to 469.913) for post-1998 investments.

headings.title: Investment in life and endowment insurance policies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7. Authorizes investing in life or endowment insurance policies on minor or insurable life, payable to minor or estate.

headings.title: Adult ownership powers and court approval for gifts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8. Grants custodian adult ownership powers over custodial property, expressly barring gifts without court approval.

headings.title: Identification and separation of custodial property

headings.title: Joint checking and savings withdrawal accounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10. Authorizes establishing checking/savings accounts allowing minor withdrawals, treated as property delivery to minor.

headings.title: Authority to borrow, lend, lease, and contract

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Permits non-donor custodian to elect reasonable annual compensation, lapsing if not affirmatively claimed during calendar year.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4. Prohibits expense or compensation claims from constituting a lien on property transferred to third persons or to minor.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9. Provides successor custodian holds property under section 404.047 without needing to designate capacity as successor.

headings.title: Duty of resigning or representative custodian to deliver property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10. Requires resigning custodian or representative of deceased custodian to promptly deliver custodial property and records.

headings.title: Court petition for custodian removal, successor, and bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11. Authorizes minor over fourteen, family member, or interested person to petition court for cause to remove custodian, require bond, or appoint successor.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3. Authorizes court upon removing custodian to order accounting, transfer property and records, and compel conveyance execution.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4. Establishes two-year limitation period following final disclosure statement, with tolling until age twenty-one or death, preserving fraud actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1985/1989 history, and 'this act' (H.B. 145, 1989) disposition-table footnote; all 4 headings retained covering accounting petitions, court validation/allocation, removal orders, and two-year limitations.

headings.title: Definitions of certification, incapacitated, and patient
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Defines "certification", "incapacitated" (inability to care for self risking serious injury/illness), and "patient" under health care act.

headings.title: Application of general power of attorney definitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Applies definitions of section 404.703 to health care act except as specifically modified.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; both headings retained covering health care POA definitions ('certification', 'incapacitated', 'patient') and incorporation of section 404.703 definitions.

headings.title: Specific grant required for withholding artificial nutrition and hydration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Requires patient to specifically grant authority in power of attorney to direct withholding/withdrawing artificial nutrition/hydration, saving physician medical intolerance judgment.

headings.title: Prohibition on withdrawing naturally ingested nutrition and hydration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Forbids attorney in fact from authorizing withdrawal of naturally ingestible nutrition or hydration with intent of causing patient death.

headings.title: Requirement to consider medical comfort care measures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3. Mandates attorneys in fact consider appropriate comfort care measures in accordance with current medical standards.

headings.title: Physician explanation or comatose certification before withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4. Requires physician to attempt explaining withdrawal and offer refusal opportunity, or certify patient is comatose/unable to comprehend in file.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; all 4 headings retained covering specific grant for artificial nutrition/hydration, prohibition on withdrawing natural nutrition/hydration, comfort care, and physician explanation or comatose certification.

headings.title: Provider conscience objection based on religious or moral beliefs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Relieves individual health care providers from duty to honor agent's decision contrary to religious beliefs or moral convictions.

headings.title: Facility conscience objection based on institutional policy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Relieves hospitals and health facilities from honoring agent decision contrary to institutional religious/moral policy unless prior notice received.

headings.title: Duty not to impede patient transfer upon conscience refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3. Mandates refusing provider or facility shall not impede attorney in fact from transferring patient to another provider or facility.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; broadened subsection 2 title to cover both religious and moral institutional policies and retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Unlawful conditioning of health care services or facility admission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Makes it unlawful for health providers or facilities to require executing durable power of attorney for health care as condition of care or admission.

headings.title: Unlawful conditioning of health insurance coverage or benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Makes it unlawful for insurers, health plans, or HMOs to require executing health care power as condition of insurance or benefits.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; both headings retained covering prohibitions on conditioning health care/facility admission or health insurance/benefits on executing a health care POA.

headings.title: Mandatory filing of power of attorney in patient medical record
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Requires copy of health care power of attorney be included in medical record upon discovery before provider acts on agent decision.

headings.title: Agent right to medical records and retention of evidentiary privileges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Grants health care agent same rights as patient to receive medical information and consent to disclosures, preserving evidentiary privileges.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; both headings retained covering mandatory inclusion of health care POA in medical record before action and agent medical-record access without waiving evidentiary privileges.

headings.title: Preservation of chapter 565 criminal provisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Clarifies nothing in health care act revokes, amends, or limits operation of chapter 565 criminal code.

headings.title: Withholding treatment not suicide, homicide, or contract invalidation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Provides death from withdrawing life-sustaining treatment under act is not suicide or homicide and does not impair or invalidate insurance or annuity contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; retained subsection 1 (chapter 565 preservation) and refined subsection 2 title from 'contract breach' to 'contract invalidation'.

headings.title: Revocation at any time and communication to agent or provider
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1991 S.B. 148). Permits patient to revoke health care power at any time in any communicable manner, effective upon communication to agent or health provider.

headings.title: Duty of provider to record revocation in medical records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2. Directs attending physician or health provider upon learning of revocation to make revocation part of patient's medical records.

headings.title: Subsequent power of attorney revoking prior health care powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3. Provides execution of valid health care power of attorney revokes prior health care powers unless instrument provides otherwise.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1991 S.B. 148 history note; all 3 headings retained covering revocation at any time upon communication, medical-record entry of revocation, and revocation by subsequent health care POA.
